Not really what you are describing is cex backend implementation and depends on how often they poll for new blocks. My change affects the average confirmation times for transactions. When you do a transaction at the moment it will not be included in the current block the miner works on. It will be in the next one. With my change the current block a miner works on gets refreshed every 20s to include new transactions from the mempool. Resulting in your transaction potentially getting mined faster

Another optimization you can try if you are open to changing the queries is using hash comparison for lookups. I have for example an index over the address using hashtext and query like this:

SELECT no.tx_id FROM node_outputs no WHERE hashtextextended(no.address, 0) = hashtextextended($1, 0) AND no.address = $1

Index is build like this:

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS "node_outputs__address_hashtext" ON node_outputs (hashtextextended(address, 0), timestamp desc, spent, tx_id);
